figureLabel: Exploring objects in our environment for sound and movement ideas
altText: Basic 1 learners collecting natural and man-made objects in their school compound while talking about their shapes, sizes, textures and the sounds they can make.
detailedDescription: A Basic 1 class in a Ghanaian school compound where small groups of children collect stones, seeds, sticks, tins and plastic bottles. They touch, shake and tap the objects while the teacher asks questions about size, shape, weight, texture and possible sounds. The scene shows learners as explorers gathering raw ideas for future music, dance and drama, not just obeying instructions.

figureLabel: Investigating how objects can be used for music, dance and drama
altText: Basic 1 learners experimenting with sticks, stones, bottles and body percussion to discover different sounds and movements for performing arts.
detailedDescription: Inside a Basic 1 classroom, children sit in circles experimenting with simple materials: two learners tap sticks together in rhythm, another pair clap and stamp their feet, others shake bottles with seeds or stones inside. The teacher helps them listen for loud and soft, fast and slow, and invites them to move their bodies in response. The focus is on curiosity and discovery, not perfect performance.

figureLabel: Sharing ideas for creating performances from everyday objects
altText: Basic 1 learners discussing and drawing simple plans on how to use collected objects to create music, dance or drama for their community.
detailedDescription: A Basic 1 class sits in small groups with a chart paper in the middle. Children point to drawings of sticks, stones, tins and bottles while suggesting how they could use them to create a short performance, such as a rhythm pattern, a simple dance or a short drama scene. The teacher listens and writes down learners’ ideas, reinforcing that their environment is full of creative possibilities and that their voices matter.

figureLabel: Improvised performance using sounds and movements from the environment
altText: Basic 1 learners performing a short piece with improvised instruments, body movements and spoken lines while classmates watch and respond.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian school compound, a small group of Basic 1 learners perform a short piece using improvised instruments made from local materials and body percussion. Some tap sticks together, others shake bottles, while a few combine simple dance steps and spoken lines. Their classmates sit as an audience, clapping lightly and giving feedback with the teacher’s guidance. The scene shows children as young creators and performers using local resources to express ideas and feelings.

figureLabel: Explaining how we created our class song
altText: Basic 1 learners in a Ghanaian classroom sitting in a circle while one child stands and explains how their group created a simple song with clapping and movement.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 1 classroom in Ghana, learners sit in a circle on low chairs. At the front, a small group stands together. One child speaks while the others nod. On the board behind them are a few key words or short phrases that formed the lyrics of their class song about keeping the school clean. The child points to the words and describes how the group chose the tune, added claps between lines and practised the movements. The teacher listens quietly and only guides with short prompts. The scene trains children to talk clearly about the creative decisions they made in music and movement, not just to perform.

figureLabel: Pair-share about our short drama
altText: Two Basic 1 learners facing each other and talking about the short drama they acted, while holding simple props like a broom and a bucket.
detailedDescription: On one side of the classroom, two Basic 1 learners sit facing each other, each holding a simple prop from their drama: one has a broom, the other a small plastic bucket. They lean forward as they talk. A small reflection card on the table between them shows three simple questions with pictures: ‘What was your drama about?’, ‘What did you enjoy most?’, ‘What will you change next time?’. In the background other pairs are also talking softly. The teacher moves around but does not interrupt. This scene builds the habit of thinking and talking about the meaning and quality of their drama, not only acting it once and forgetting.

figureLabel: Using a simple process chart to talk about our work
altText: Basic 1 teacher and learners standing beside a simple four-step process chart showing how they planned, practised, improved and performed their music or drama.
detailedDescription: At the front of the room, a large manila sheet hangs on the wall with four boxes labelled in child-friendly language: ‘1. We got ideas’, ‘2. We practised’, ‘3. We improved’, ‘4. We performed’. Simple pictures inside each box show children thinking, practising, correcting and performing. A Basic 1 learner stands beside the chart, pointing to each box while explaining how their group followed the steps to create a dance about washing hands. Other children listen. The teacher occasionally asks, ‘Which part was easiest?’ or ‘Where did you struggle most?’ and writes short answers. The scene helps learners see creative work as a repeatable process they can describe and improve, not magic.

figureLabel: Feedback circle after a performance
altText: A small group of Basic 1 pupils who just performed a short song-and-dance sit in the middle of a circle while classmates give simple, positive feedback using sentence starters on a chart.
detailedDescription: In the centre of the classroom, four Basic 1 pupils who have just performed a short song-and-dance sit on a bench. Around them, the rest of the class forms a circle on the floor. On the wall is a chart with simple sentence starters and smiley icons: ‘I liked…’, ‘I noticed…’, ‘Next time you can…’. One child in the circle raises a hand and says, ‘I liked the way you used your hands to show the rain’. Another adds, ‘Next time you can sing a little louder’. The performers smile and respond briefly about how they practised that part. The teacher guides the tone to stay kind and helpful. The picture trains children to give and receive gentle feedback on performing arts, building confidence and reflective skills.

figureLabel: Reflecting on local performing arts
altText: Basic 1 learners in Ghana watching a small group of local drummers and dancers performing in the school compound while a teacher helps them notice sounds and movements.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian school compound, a local group of drummers and dancers performs for a Basic 1 class. The children sit on benches or on the ground, watching carefully. Some point at the drums, others look at the dancers’ feet and hand movements. The teacher stands nearby asking gentle questions, helping them notice rhythm, tempo, costumes and expressions. The scene shows learners observing local performing arts as an important part of their culture, not just entertainment.

figureLabel: Discussing feelings and messages in performances
altText: Basic 1 learners sitting in a circle with their teacher, talking about how a local performance made them feel and what message it carried.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 1 classroom, learners sit in a circle with their teacher after watching a local performance. In the centre is a simple drawing of drummers and dancers. One child speaks while pointing at the drawing, explaining how the performance made them feel proud and happy. Another mentions that the song reminded them to work together or keep the community clean. The teacher writes key words like ‘happy’, ‘proud’, ‘warning’, ‘togetherness’ on a chart. The scene shows children learning to talk about feelings and messages in performing arts.

figureLabel: Comparing different performing arts forms
altText: Basic 1 pupils comparing pictures of a cultural troupe, a church choir and a school drama group, noting similarities and differences.
detailedDescription: On a classroom board, three simple pictures show a cultural troupe dancing with drums, a church choir singing in robes, and a school drama group acting a short scene. Basic 1 learners sit close, some pointing at the pictures. The teacher leads them to mention what is similar and different: costumes, movements, instruments, and the kinds of messages each performance gives. The scene trains learners to compare performing arts forms thoughtfully rather than treating them all as the same.

figureLabel: Planning how to use local performing arts in class
altText: Basic 1 learners working in small groups to plan how they could use local songs, rhythms or dances in their own classroom performances.
detailedDescription: Several small groups of Basic 1 learners sit around low tables with chart paper. On each chart are simple drawings and short words representing local songs, drum patterns, clapping games and dances. Children discuss and point at ideas while the teacher moves between groups. One group plans to use a local clapping game as an introduction to their performance; another chooses a simple folk song for the ending. The image highlights children as planners, deciding how to adapt local performing arts for their own class work.

figureLabel: Planning a simple performing arts sequence
altText: Basic 1 learners planning a short performance on chart paper, arranging pictures for beginning, middle and ending.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 1 classroom, a small group of learners sits around a table with a large sheet divided into three boxes labelled ‘Beginning’, ‘Middle’ and ‘Ending’. They place small drawings or picture cards showing singing, clapping, simple dance steps and a short closing bow. The teacher kneels beside them, asking which part should come first and what should happen at the end. The scene shows children planning a simple, clear sequence for a performing arts piece, thinking like young directors.

figureLabel: Rehearsing with voice, movement and instruments
altText: Basic 1 learners rehearsing a short performance using singing, clapping, simple dance steps and improvised instruments.
detailedDescription: A group of Basic 1 pupils rehearses in the classroom. Some sing a simple song, others clap in rhythm and a few use improvised instruments like shakers, tins and small drums. They stand in a loose line practising moving forwards together and then stepping back. The teacher stands at the side, counting the beat and reminding them to watch one another. The atmosphere is focused but joyful, showing rehearsal as a time for teamwork, listening and practice rather than a rushed performance.

figureLabel: Performing for a class audience
altText: Basic 1 learners presenting a short music and movement piece to their classmates acting as a respectful audience.
detailedDescription: At the front of the classroom, a group of Basic 1 children performs a short piece that combines singing, clapping and simple dance steps. They stand confidently, looking towards their classmates. The rest of the class sits as an audience, watching quietly with a few smiling and clapping at the end. The teacher is nearby, pleased but not dominating the scene. The picture emphasises that performance is part of learning, with both performers and audience practising respect and concentration.

figureLabel: Reflecting on performance and feedback
altText: Basic 1 performers and their classmates using simple feedback cards to talk about what went well and what to improve in a performance.
detailedDescription: After a performance, the Basic 1 performers sit at the front while their classmates and teacher sit facing them. Some audience members hold simple feedback cards with smiley faces and words like ‘clear voice’, ‘working together’, and ‘more practice’. One child in the audience speaks kindly about what they liked, while a performer nods and smiles. The teacher writes a few agreed points on a small reflection chart. The scene builds a habit of kind, specific feedback and continuous improvement.

figureLabel: Choosing everyday situations for drama
altText: Basic 1 learners and their teacher seated in a circle, choosing everyday situations from a chart in the middle to act out as drama.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian Basic 1 classroom, the teacher and pupils sit in a circle on low chairs or a mat. In the centre lies a large sheet divided into boxes with simple sketches and words: a family eating together, children sweeping the compound, someone refusing to litter, pupils crossing the road safely, and a child saying sorry. Learners point at the sketches and suggest which situations to turn into short dramas. The teacher listens and writes key words like ‘family’, ‘cleaning’, ‘road safety’ on a small card. The atmosphere is full of ideas, showing children choosing relevant everyday situations for drama.

figureLabel: Practising voice, facial expression and movement
altText: Basic 1 learners in groups practising short drama scenes, using clear voices, expressive faces and simple body movements.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, several groups of Basic 1 learners rehearse different drama scenes. In the foreground, two children act a ‘saying sorry’ scene, with one looking worried then relieved, and the other showing surprise then forgiveness. In the background, another pair practises crossing an imaginary road with exaggerated looking left and right, while another group mimics sweeping and singing. The teacher moves between groups, modelling how to change voice, facial expression and movement to show feelings. The scene emphasises practice and experimentation, not perfection.

figureLabel: Performing short drama pieces
altText: Basic 1 learners performing a short drama about keeping the environment clean while their classmates watch as an audience.
detailedDescription: On a simple ‘stage’ area in the school compound or classroom, a small group of Basic 1 learners acts a drama about keeping the environment clean. One child is about to throw rubbish on the ground; another stops them and points clearly to a dustbin. After a short argument, the first child agrees and uses the bin. Their gestures and faces show change of mind. The rest of the class sits as a respectful audience, watching and clapping at the end. The teacher stands aside, observing and ready to guide reflection.

figureLabel: Reflecting on and improving drama performances
altText: Basic 1 drama performers and their classmates having a reflection discussion after a performance, suggesting what went well and what to improve.
detailedDescription: Back in the classroom, the children who just performed a drama sit at the front on a bench, while the rest of the class sits facing them in a semi-circle. One performer uses hand gestures to explain what was easy or difficult. A child in the audience raises a hand to give friendly feedback, and another reads from a simple feedback card. The teacher stands beside a flipchart headed ‘What went well / Next time we will…’, writing short phrases suggested by the children. The scene shows a safe space where learners think together about how to make future dramas clearer and stronger.
